request.prompt:
WALDPOST CANONICAL ILLUSTRATION STYLE — waldpost-watercolour-pencil-v1

Use the supplied canonical animals.png and objects.png reference images as the authority for drawing technique. They show the predominant style of the current Waldpost gallery. Match their actual pixels, not an imagined style suggested by a filename.

Draw warm children's picture-book watercolour finished with visible coloured-pencil strokes. Use light, gently uneven washes, organic sepia contours, delicate hatching, softly irregular edges and modest drawn shading. Surfaces look painted and pencilled, with paper grain within the illustration. Keep the warmth of cream, honey brown, restrained sage and blue, while preserving every exact colour required by a task. Subjects remain friendly, recognizable and anatomically believable.

Do not turn the drawing into a 3D render, plush toy, clay or felt craft, photograph, glossy object, embossed surface or studio-lit miniature. Avoid deep ambient-occlusion shadows, inflated forms and realistic material microtexture. Do not mix in another illustration technique or use historical artwork as a style reference.

The role instructions below set the necessary detail and composition within this one style. Learning pictures retain fine drawn contours; small navigation symbols use the approved simpler, broader shapes and flat fills in the same palette. Keep the existing rendered game-character identities separate from image-generated learning subjects. Exact geometry and handwriting remain authored paths.

Preserve subject identity, counted quantities, exact answer colours and action differences. Use real alpha for isolated pictures and stationery, and an opaque canvas only when the selected role requires a scene or branding image. No accidental background, halo, visible grid, labels or extra objects.

ROLE: learning
Match the canonical watercolour and coloured-pencil technique closely: fine organic contours, uneven washes and gentle drawn volume. Keep accurate species, action contrasts, one counted object per item and exact answer colours. Use transparent square cells, generous gutters and complete silhouettes.

FRAMING AND EDGE QUALITY:
Compare related pictures side by side at the size used in the game. For square cells, draw the complete silhouette with enough transparent space to pack it centred on both axes, with its longest visible side about 80% of the cell. Keep its proportions and use comparable visual weight for neighbouring answers. Reuse the same painting when a subject and pose recur. Leave genuine alpha around every isolated subject and retain the soft pencil edges. Inspect on light and dark backgrounds for pale matte, clipped outlines, stray pixels and neighbouring subjects. In a cell repair, preserve the pixels and positions of the other cells. Scenes and irregular layouts follow their role and brief.

ATTACH THESE ACTUAL IMAGE FILES IN THIS ORDER:
1. design/illustrations/references/watercolour-pencil-v1/animals.png — canonical-style: canonical drawing technique for animals; fixed majority-style pixels
2. design/illustrations/references/watercolour-pencil-v1/objects.png — canonical-style: canonical drawing technique for objects, leaves and flowers; fixed majority-style pixels

SUBJECT AND LAYOUT BRIEF:
Create a NEW extension sheet for the Waldpost woodland learning-picture library. Match the two supplied canonical reference images in their warm watercolour and visible coloured-pencil finish. These are isolated learning pictures, suitable for later vocabulary, sorting, matching, observation and sequence puzzles. No labels, text, numerals, frames, badges, faces on objects or decorative extras.

LAYOUT: a square canvas divided into EXACTLY 4 equal columns and 4 equal rows (16 equal square cells). Draw exactly 15 independent complete subjects in row-major order below. Leave row 4 column 4 completely transparent. Each subject stays inside its own square with at least 12% clear space on each side. Centre each subject in its cell; keep every ear, root, handle, tail and wing intact. No overlapping cells, ground plane or backdrop. Genuine alpha zero around all paintings, including open handles; no painted checkerboard or paper rectangle. Gentle pencil texture remains inside the subject.

Row 1, column 1: squirrel-dig (Eichhörnchen gräbt) — one red squirrel digging a small shallow hole with its forepaws, tail raised, a tiny earth patch only.
Row 1, column 2: squirrel-climb (Eichhörnchen klettert) — one red squirrel climbing vertically on a short isolated tree trunk segment.
Row 1, column 3: hedgehog-curl (Igel rollt sich ein) — one hedgehog curled into a closed prickly ball, no face or legs visible.
Row 1, column 4: hedgehog-sniff (Igel schnuppert) — one hedgehog with nose lowered close to one leaf, four paws grounded.
Row 2, column 1: badger-dig (Dachs gräbt) — one black-and-white European badger digging with its front paws, tiny earth patch only.
Row 2, column 2: roe-graze (Reh frisst Gras) — one roe deer with head lowered to a tiny tuft of grass.
Row 2, column 3: roe-rest (Reh ruht) — one roe deer lying down with legs folded beneath its body and head upright.
Row 2, column 4: frog-swim (Frosch schwimmt) — one green frog seen from above swimming with hind legs extended and forelegs forward, no water background.
Row 3, column 1: owl-fly (Eule fliegt) — one tawny owl in flight with wings outstretched symmetrically.
Row 3, column 2: robin-sing (Rotkehlchen singt) — one robin singing with its beak visibly open and chest raised, no musical notes.
Row 3, column 3: woodpecker-peck (Specht klopft) — one great spotted woodpecker holding onto a short isolated trunk segment, bill touching bark.
Row 3, column 4: beaver-gnaw (Biber nagt) — one beaver gnawing a short wooden branch held between forepaws, broad flat tail visible.
Row 4, column 1: otter-swim (Fischotter schwimmt) — one European otter swimming horizontally with long tail extended, two small water ripples only.
Row 4, column 2: duck-dive (Ente taucht) — one mallard dabbling head-down, rump and orange webbed feet above two small water ripples.
Row 4, column 3: fox-listen (Fuchs lauscht) — one red fox standing still, ears pricked and head tilted attentively, no accessories.

Row 4, column 4: EMPTY, fully transparent. Use a consistent woodland picture-book scale; keep shapes clear and recognizable at 80–120 pixels. All names and IDs above are instructions only and must never be drawn.

STYLE PRIORITY: The brief changes subjects and layout only. Keep waldpost-watercolour-pencil-v1 and the supplied canonical reference technique throughout; do not import the style of a composition-only reference.
